Labels: MEASURED = run by us with the shipped program's counters or with the named tool; DERIVED = arithmetic from stated numbers; CITED = measured and published by the named earlier entry.

## 1. Target and output
- **Target.** `sha256-r39-prefix-v1`: SHA-256 with the first 39 steps in every compression, standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all 256 output bits.
- **Output.** Two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1': the same random first block M0, second blocks with M1' = M1 + DL (word-wise modular, differences in words 8..12). Equal lengths, identical padding block. Ordinary collision.
- **Claim.** time_log2 = 94.0669, memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000, preprocessing_log2 = 43, advice 160 bytes = 2^7.32193, success probability 0.39. The time is total charged work (work cap, one-time setup, 2^43 preprocessing), ceiled at the fourth decimal; the memory is the peak over the phases of the run, 1,013,609 bytes, plus 32,768 bytes of headroom, claimed at 2^20.

## 2. The construction
**2.1 Advice.** The 39-step semi-free-start pair of 5f8e6192 (CV_PUB, MP_PUB, M_PUB; 160 bytes), on the characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 Tables 21 and 23 (CITED from 293ca62c and 38912d66). No recipe is shipped: the advice is the 160-byte pair only.

**2.2 The transplant, k = 4.** As in w13: fix A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 to the advice values; for any cv and (a0, a1, a2, a3) = A[4..7] the words W0..W11 follow (`k4_words`). W9 = C - a1 + h4(a2, a3) with h4 = MAJ(A8, a3, a2) - CH(E12, E11, E10), E10 = a2 + t(a3), E11 = a3 + c11; W10 = kappa(a3) - a2; W11 depends on a3 only; W0 and W1 do not depend on (a2, a3).

**2.3 The fibre is a parameter.** On any fibre h4(a2, a3) = h, W9 = C - a1 + h is one value per claw, F9 stays a per-claw test, and W16 = s1(W14) + W9 + s0(W1) + W0 is one value per claw. Taking h = FIB = 0x3cc9eebe instead of the advice's h0 = 0x36faf0de shifts the walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 by K4_HD = FIB - h0 = 0x05cefde0 (computed by the program from the advice). A claw of the shifted walk map then gives W16 = g for every entry of the new list. The advice (a2, a3) itself is not on the new fibre, so the base variant is not a trial and its path is removed from `claw()`; the transplant-claw experiment no longer claws the advice (an h0 claw). MEASURED on the built program (build/e2e15.py, from w15/tools/check15s.py): all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1014 of the shipped program x 20 listed entries each, 35,940 (claw, entry) cases: W1 = u, W16 = g, W9 = C9 + HD - a1 in F9, both messages on the advice trail through step 16, the advice states after step 17 at a W17 hit; failures none.

**2.4 What remains after a claw.** Per claw: W9 in F9. Per entry: W8 in F8 (density 9/128), and W17 = advice value; then the tail (Section 8). Two entries with the same a2 and kappa (mates) pass or fail W17 together; they differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word.

**2.5 The list by rule (MEASURED and DERIVED).**
- Classes: a3 = (E11adv XOR m) - c11 for every submask m of CUBE = 0xf74400da (14 bits, 16,384 masks), kept when W11C - a3 lies in F11: 1,536 candidates. CUBE is the OR of the E11 masks of the 728 classes of the exhaustive enumeration; the rule R2 of our list-ceiling note (E11 AND 0x08b81020 fixed) holds on the whole cube because the two masks are disjoint.
- Entries of a class: every a2 with (R3) h4(a2, a3) = FIB, (R4) W10 = kappa(a3) - a2 in F10, (R5) bit 30 of E10 equal to bit 30 of E11.
- **The rule set equals the exhaustive list.** enum15 scans all 2^32 values of a3 and checks every candidate entry on the real two-message trail at the advice point and three random points (0 mixed verdicts, 0 failures of every identity it checks; 9,701,592 valid entries in 728 classes). build/rule15.c generates the rule set and compares it with that list as sorted (a3, a2) sets: equal; at h0 the same rule gives exactly the 821,520-entry list of f92b8068.
- F10 is a set of bit conditions on W10 (D10 = 0xc0000000, T10 = 0x087ff000): w2^w13 = 1, w9^w26 = 1, w15 = w19, and either w30 = 1, or w30 = 0 with w3^w14 = w10^w27 = w31 = 1^w16^w20. Checked over all 2^32 values: 301,989,888 members, 0 mismatches.
- **Generator.** A bit-serial automaton over a2 (the fibre's carry and borrow, the borrow of kappa - a2, the captured W10 bits, the F10 branch) is solved backwards, bit-sliced over 256 candidate classes per 256-bit word (`_k4fe`); then a depth-first search with exact pruning lists the 18-bit prefixes of each class (`_k4lf`). Classes are taken in kappa order, and a group's prefix set becomes 18 bit planes per block of 256 lanes when the next group begins (`_k4fin`). One sample entry per group is kept for the planted checks.
- **Table.** 200 kappa groups, 728 classes (at most 8 per group), 62,400 prefixes in 300 blocks (at most 1,024 prefixes per group). MEASURED: group by group, the prefix sets built at import equal those of the exhaustive list, and every sample entry satisfies the rule. Counts asserted at import.

## 3. The W17 pass
**3.1 The equation.** As in w13: s0(y) = y + r with y = a2 + w and r = kd + W17 - u - w; the low 18 bits of y determine the other 14, and 18 bit checks remain.

**3.2 The pass (`k4q`).** The routine of w13, unchanged except two lines (Section 3.4). Per evaluated F9 claw: spill and restore (624), a1 and w (55), the 18 constant words (54); per group 110; per block 403. **K4_PASS = 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks) = 143,633, the same for every claw**, asserted at import. A survivor costs 711 plus 563 per class of its group tested: at most 711 + 563 x 8 = 5,215. A key hit tests the classes of its group as mates: at most 8 x (560 + 2 x 2,812) = 49,472.

**3.3 Same hits.** A listed key satisfies W17 in a claw if and only if its prefix lane survives and the scalar test accepts it. MEASURED by the gate on 6 real F9 claws of the shipped program's windows: for each of the 200 groups a planted key (the group's sample entry, its W17 placed as the target) is found by the pass, and the counted cost is the group's pass cost plus 711 + 563 x (classes tested) per survivor. The organizer experiment repeats it for all 200 groups on the first F9 claw of each window (Section 11).

**3.4 Changes against w13.** (i) The fibre: c9, C9 shifted; k4q's W9 reference is the claw's own W9, C9 + HD - a1, not the advice's; the mates of a key hit are the classes of its group, not the 4,096 submasks of 0xf1c000da. (ii) The list by rule: no recipe literal, no inflate reader, no decoder; the per-key diagnostic runs over the entries of every 50th group (four groups) and only in the experiment modes. (iii) The walk table: 97 x 1,024 = 99,328 slots of 40 bits, 15,520 words, the largest table under 2^20 with the other rows of Section 6. The slot of a 25-bit distinguished value r is (97 r) >> 15 = ((r << 6) + (r << 5) + r) >> 15 through the counter; 2^15 / 97 = 338 < 512, so slot and the 9 check bits determine r. Keep-longer rule as in w13.

**3.5 Routine by routine against w13** (every routine of the source compared; module lines with constants are listed in Section 5). Changed: `consts` (c9 + K4_HD); `Attack.base_setup` (only C9, shifted, is left); `Attack.claw` (the base-variant path removed; check mode asserts the claw's W9 against a listed entry); `Attack.hit` (slot (97 r) >> 15 and its check); `P` (WDIG of 15,520 words); `k4q` (the claw's W9; mates among the group's classes); `k4f` (the diagnostic over the four groups of `_k4ind`); `_k4fin` (planes of one group from its prefix set); `k4_budget` (G and the second-order divisor 1 - 0.07579); `_e1` (transplant-claw: advice checks and the fibre checks per group; random transplants with a listed entry); `_k4e` (no base F8 count; the acceptance constants). Removed: `_w3gen`, `_k4c1`, `_sm`. Added: `_k4st`, `_k4fe`, `_k4lf`, `_k4cls`, `_k4build`, `_k4ind`, `h4ok`. Every other routine is byte-identical to w13's. This entry against 0b62ed88: `P` (SCREEN = 1, KCAP = 679, KCAP0 = 710 for the screen-off path, DTRY = 8,192), `k4_scr` (added), `Attack.__init__` (the screen flag), `Attack.window_setup` (the screen in the draw loop, Section 3.6), `K4_OPS_PER_CLAW`, `k4_budget` and the import assertion (Section 5), `_k4e` (the four asserted windows run with the screen off; trial 0 adds one screened window, Section 11).

**3.6 Pre-generation screen (credited to 0xplemonade's a3eb4a8a; its masks, threshold, KCAP = 679 and DTRY = 8,192 unchanged).** Each drawn first block's chaining value is scored before kernel generation: from `consts5` of the CV (cw, eb, P, R; 4 ops to pack), S = 3 pop(R & 0x00F27618) + 2 pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6) + 2 eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] - pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), charged 183 ops per draw, a3eb4a8a's counted figure, kept here as a conservative charge above an explicit v5 form of at most 65 ops: with A = pop(R & 0x00F27618), B = pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6), C = pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), each count is the SWAR sequence x -= (x >> 1) & 0x55555555 (3); x = (x & 0x33333333) + ((x >> 2) & 0x33333333) (4); x = (x + (x >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f (3); x += x >> 8 (2); x += x >> 16 (2); x &= 63 (1), 15 ops, so 3 counts plus 3 input masks = 48; eb[1], eb[2], P[31] extracted in 5; 3A, 2B, 2eb[1] in 4; the nonnegative S + 28 = 3A + 2B + 2eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] + (28 - C) formed and compared, branch included, in at most 8. The program's host bit count, bin().count('1'), evaluates the same predicate; it is not a charged unit op, and the 183 charged ops per draw exceed the 65. A block with S > 5 is discarded (3 more ops) and the next block is drawn (its draw and first-block compression charged as before); a kept block goes to the unchanged exact kernel gate, which now accepts at most 679 records (KCAP; 710 in the base). A window stops after 8,192 discarded draws or 32 rejected generations, every charge counted. The screen consumes no randomness. Its effect on work enters the price only through the re-measured window totals (H6, Appendix B) and C_W; its effect on the window law and the trial count is the new premise H1-screen (Section 10).

- **Claimed: memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000.** The peak over the three phases is the walk phase, 1,013,609 bytes; with 32,768 bytes of headroom that is 1,046,377 bytes, within 2^20. (This entry's audit of the shipped program finds the attack-state row 96 bytes above the 3,872 that ae2d3c1c carried from 0b62ed88: the `screen` attribute and the discard counter's key and value in the `st` dictionary, three items of 32 bytes; corrected here in the G and W phases.) The program asserts 32 x (table + queue + planes) + 315,465 + 32,768 <= 2^20. A table of 98 x 1,024 slots would not fit.
- **Phases** as in w13. S is the import: module data, code and the generator's working memory; when the import returns no generator, feasibility table or builder frame is alive and no attack object exists (MEASURED, audit with the cycle collector off). G and W as in w13, re-audited on this program. Phase W exceeds G by 503,630 and S by 357,448 bytes. The row total is not a memory state.
- **Rows.** Walk rows and the 4,111-instruction walk census as in w13 (CITED from 9993eaa8 there; this program's executed-block census does not exceed w13's). The prefix table: 300 x 18 x 32 = 172,800 bytes of planes plus lane counts, group constants, 728 class words and 200 sample keys. The setup rows are measured on the generator (build/genmem15.py): largest feasibility table of a 256-lane chunk 1,947 lane words and 14,673 key scalars, transition memo at most 213 keys and 285 children, search stack 16, largest group 1,024 prefixes. No recipe, decoder or inflate row remains. The walk-kernel generator rows are the maxima over 300 random chaining values (776 graph records, 11,451 characters); run on the chaining values of all 48 shipped windows the generator stays below them (710 records, 10,567 characters). Phase G lies 503,630 bytes under phase W, so the generator rows would have to grow about tenfold to move the peak.
- **Code.** Every k4 instruction has a row, at 36 bytes: one instruction per syntactic operation of every k4 routine, the generator and the experiment diagnostics included (1,346), plus the pass in looped machine form (1,246): 2,592 instructions.
- **What the table covers.** All memory the `--attack` path allocates, setup included, and all k4 code. The screen (Section 3.6) keeps only the scalars of one draw (four packed words and S, 20 bytes, transient), inside the 32,768-byte headroom; the kernel-image rows stay at 710 records, above the screened path's KCAP = 679. The experiment modes allocate on top of it the diagnostic's entry blocks and statistics; the `--attack` path never allocates them.

## 7. Success probability and the cap
- **Trials (this entry).** A trial is a listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9. Mates of a key (the entries with the same a2 and kappa) share W17 and differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word from W18 on (Section 2.4). When a key hits W17 the program tests every class of its group, so every mate passing F8 is compressed. Let T_j be the event that entry j's pair collides along the advice differences (the event the tail replica counts) and U_k the union of T_j over the F8-passing mates of key k; the key succeeds on U_k. Second-order Bonferroni inside the key: P(U_k) >= sum_j P(T_j) - sum over mate pairs i < j of P(T_i and T_j); the pair term is bounded below (the mate term); no independence between mates is assumed.
- **Count: 10679.3 per distinct claw (screened panel windows, MEASURED; a26bcf74's joint bound form).** Trials are F8-passing entries. On the 2,000 real F9 claws of the screened windows 802000-802015, the only windows of a26bcf74's 60-window panel with an entries count (16 batches of 125: the first 125 F9 claws, in arrival order, of each window; the walk and its claws are those of the attack path, window 802000 reproducing a26bcf74's Appendix B row), the listed entries passing F8 number 680,755.1 per F9 claw (s.e. 1,893.5 from the batch means; per-claw s.d. 72,662); the same claws have 575,154.9 distinct keys with an entry in F8 (1.1836 entries per key). The distinct F9 claws per window are a26bcf74's: 60 screened windows, mean 907.1667, s.d. 25.6780. Joint one-sided 99% lower bound (union bound, 99.5% on each factor; independent windows and batches, Student-t), as a26bcf74: T >= (680,755.1 - t(15, 0.995) x 1,893.5) x (907.1667 - t(59, 0.995) x 25.6780 / sqrt(60)) / 57,003.18 = 675,175.54 x 898.3429 / 57,003.18 = 10640.44 (d3a46ae6); with this entry's cap the F9 factor is the same bound on min(D_i, 944) over 1,080 predeclared windows of the same program law, all run at the cap 944 (802060-803139, Appendix D), 901.6269 with t(1079, 0.995), giving 10679.34, priced 10679.3; with t(15, 0.995) = 2.946713, t(59, 0.995) = 2.661759 (d3a46ae6's 60 windows: 10640.4) t(419, 0.995) = 2.587614 (d049ec74's 420 windows: 10658.9), t(779, 0.995) = 2.582155 (ab09e983's 780 windows: 10671.5) and t(1079, 0.995) = 2.580393 (this entry's 1,080 windows: 10679.3); priced as 10679.3 (rounded down; rule out/RULE_w18_trials.txt). C_W = 57,003.18 is the declared H1-screen model mean, as in B and the cap. One-way ANOVA of the 2,000 claws' entry counts over their 16 windows: F = 1.362 on 15 and 1,984 df. Taking the first claws of a window is not a selection on the count: on all F9 claws of windows 802000 and 802001 the first 125 average 677,197.7 and 676,356.3 entries against 681,901.6 and 683,853.0 for the rest (Welch z = -0.69, -1.17). Counted by w15/tools/f8count.exe over the exhaustive list, which equals the rule set (Section 2.5). (a26bcf74 priced 9044.1 keys per distinct claw on 0b62ed88's unscreened claws; that keys figure is not used here.)
- **The mate term (premise H7-mate-row19: an exhaustive enumeration plus the named premise H-W3-uniform, tested by the organizer).** T_j requires the advice XOR state differences at every row 18..38, so P(T_i and T_j) <= P(T_i) P(S_j | T_i), S_j the event that mate j follows them through row 19. Facts, each checked on real hits: for a hit and every mate on the same claw, the states through row 17 equal the advice's (W12..W17 are the advice words; k4_words fixes A8..A11 and E12..E15); a mate differs from the hit in a3 -> b3 only, so with d = b3 - a3, W3' = W3 + d, W11' = W11 - d and W18' - W18 = Delta(W3, d) = s0(W3 + d) - s0(W3) - d (252 of 252 real mates), while W19' = W19. P is the set of W18 values that admit the advice differences through row 19 (state 17 fixed; the explicit row-18 and row-19 conditions are the predicate P() printed in Appendix D); by enumeration of all 2^32 values |P| = 65,536, and every hit's W18 is in P. A mate with offset d can pass row 19 only if Delta(W3, d) lies in D = P - P (|D| = 9,427,275), i.e. only if the hit's W3 lies in B_d = {W3 : Delta(W3, d) in D, Delta != 0}. The list gives 20 offsets d; over all 2^32 W3, B_d is empty for 14 of them, has 30,256 elements for 2 and 120,832 for 4 (543,840 in all; Appendix D prints the enumeration program). **Pricing under H-W3-uniform.** Let X_i be the number of F8-passing mates of i through row 19; a key has at most 7 other mates, and mate j passes only if W3_i lies in B_{d_j}. Premise H-W3-uniform: given a hit, its W3 is uniform over 2^32. Then E[X_i | T_i] = sum_j P(S_j | T_i) <= sum_j P(W3_i in B_{d_j} | T_i) <= 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = 1.9693e-04 = eps, and eps/2 = 0.000099 enters the divisor; no independence between mates is assumed. **The organizer test of the premise** (the r39-mate manifest prediction, from the W3 of the 14 organizer-executed runs, pinned by their organizer-recorded observation digest48 and printed in Appendix E): of 1,888 hits in 867 carrier clusters, the organizer hits contain 0 W3 values in the union (expected 0.24 under the premise; falsified at 3 or more), and their per-bit chi-square is 24.7 on 32 df (falsified at 62.49, the 99.9% point). **The price without the premise (disclosed, not priced):** a hit-weighted bound needing no premise on W3 treats each cluster as one trial (with mean probability q_c over its hits, the chance that a cluster shows no such W3 cannot exceed 1 - q_c, reached when its hits' events coincide; cluster probabilities free; clusters, distinct carriers, independent); the largest hit-weighted P(W3 in the union | T) consistent with zero events at 99% (maximise sum_c m_c q_c / H subject to prod_c (1 - q_c) >= 0.01) is 0.01716, so eps = 7 x 0.01716 = 0.12015, eps/2 = 0.060077, divisor 1 - 0.137206 and time 94.1835, above a26bcf74's 94.1664, which is why the premise is named. The per-cluster form 4.605 / 867 = 0.00531 and the per-hit form 4.605 / 1,888 = 0.00244 are not used: the first bounds the mean over clusters, not over hits, and the second treats clustered hits as independent. The traced mates: 638 F8-passing mates, first deviation at row 18 for 335 and row 19 for 303, none later; the participant arms of 9054e0c4, re-run with carrier keys (w17/tools/matejoint2.py; 25,221 hits), have none past row 19.

- **Success: second-order Bonferroni over all key hits (counting every hit, as a7b383d1 does; credited for that only).** (i) The program tests every W17 key hit of every window: `k4q` (experiments/r39joint_k4.py lines 1042-1057) runs over every survivor lane of every group, and at each key hit compresses every class of the group whose words pass W9, W17 and F8 (lines 1050-1056, 560 per class and 2 x 2,812 per compressed pair, inside the window's counted work and priced in K as key-hit work); after a hit without collision the loops continue, and a window stops early only on a collision (line 804). At most m_max = 944 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (this entry's cap; d3a46ae6: 1,024) (`k4d`, line 1106). (ii) For a key k with an F8-passing mate in the claw let p'_k = P(U_k | claws), U_k the union of its F8-passing mates' events T_j (Trials); U_k is contained in the key's success, because the program compresses every mate. (iii) Given the hits, the window succeeds with probability at least P(union over hit k of U_k) >= sum over hits of p'_k - sum over hit pairs k < l of P(U_k and U_l) (second-order Bonferroni, for any number H of hits). Each pair term is at most min(p'_k, p'_l) <= (p'_k + p'_l) / 2, whatever the joint law of the tails, so the pair sum is at most sum over hit k of p'_k x (number of other hit keys) / 2. The p'_k are the exact probabilities of the events in the union; a lower bound on them is substituted only after (iv), where each p'_k carries the coefficient q (1 - c2 - 0.001341) > 0. (iv) Average over the hits given the claws (H5): each trial key is hit with probability q = 2^-32; keys of different claws are hit independently; inside one claw W17 = G(a2, kappa, w) + c(claw) with w and c fixed by the claw, so two keys of a claw are hit together exactly when their G values coincide, which the program-independent count sweep/cohit.c measures at 1.336 times the independent pair rate (512 random w, all 3,462,264 keys). Hence E[pair sum | claws] <= sum over k of p'_k [q^2 (n_w - D_c(k)) + q pi_k] / 2, with D_c(k) the trial keys of k's claw and pi_k its expected co-hit partners in that claw. The cross-claw part is q^2 sum over claws c of P_c (m_w - 1) mu_D after averaging the other claws' key counts, which are functions of their own (a0, a1) only and i.i.d. across the claws of a window (H1-screen): since m_w <= m_max by the program, it is at most q^2 (m_max - 1) mu_D P_w for ANY dependence between the number of claws and the tails, with mu_D <= 579,271 (the 99% bound, rounded up of the keys per claw, 576,745 + 2.602 x 970). Within a claw, both keys of a pair hit iff their G values coincide. The Bonferroni sum is taken over the sub-collection of hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has at most 4 keys; a union over fewer events is still a lower bound, and the choice depends on the claw's (w, c) only, not on any tail. For a kept key N_k(w) <= 3, so its pair term is (q/2) p'_k min(N_k(w), 3). Averaged over w (independent of the tails, H5) it is at most (q/2) p'_k pi_max with pi_max = 1.36e-2, the family-wise bound (alpha = 0.001, all keys, two runs of 16,384 random w: 1.3556e-02 and 1.3355e-02) on E[min(N_k, 3)] for every listed key. The left-out hits lose at most q p'_k P(N_k >= 4) of the first-order term, with P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 0.001341 for every key (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise at alpha = 0.001). Participant tools: w15/sweep/cohit2.c (output w15/sweep/cohit2_16384.txt), w15/sweep/cohit3.c (w15/sweep/cohit3_16384.txt), w15/sweep/nf.c (w15/sweep/nf.txt: s0(y) - y has at most 14 preimages, so N_k(w) <= 2,799; not needed by the bound). Both terms are bounded for every key, so they hold whatever the correlation between partner rates and tails across keys. c2 = 2^-32 x 1,023 x 579,271 / 2 + 1.36e-2 / 2 = 0.068988 + 0.006800 = 0.075788, a26bcf74's divisor is 1 - c2 - 0.001341 = 1 - 0.077129, and with the mate term (Trials; eps/2 = 0.000099, Section 7) the divisor is 1 - 0.071734 - 0.000099 = 1 - 0.071833 (a26bcf74's 0.077129 with the cross-claw term at m_max = 944, 0.063592 in place of 0.068988) ((1 - a)(1 - b) >= 1 - a - b). No moment of the window size, no correlation and no allowance enters. Over windows, E[q P_w] >= E[n_w] q (1 - eps/2) p_entry, n_w the trial entries of the window and p_entry the entry tail weighted by trial entries (H2-entries); the sum over a key's mates of P(T_j) is at most P(U_k) (1 + eps/2) by the mate term. (v) Windows are independent (fresh first blocks): P(no success) <= product over windows of (1 - P(window success)) <= exp(-lambda). No hit is selected or ordered; every hit enters symmetrically; the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits. Hence lambda = B x G x 10679.3 x 2^-32 x 2^-74.4783 x (1 - 0.071833) = -ln 0.61 + 2^-40, set in `k4_budget`; success 0.39. The divisor costs 0.1160 bit. (vi) Real W17 hits at probability 2^-32 were observed: the 48 windows had 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over all 200 groups (dispersion chi-square 34.35 on 47 df); of them, 3 F8-passing mates were compressed against 6.85 expected (Poisson P = 0.09, adverse and not significant; disclosed).
- **The work cap (H6, screened whole-window bound, on 1,080 windows).** The cap is set from the measured totals of whole screened windows, not from per-component bounds: a window's total is the shipped counter `m.o` over `Attack.run_window()` (every screen draw and discard, the base walk, the k4d gate and insertion, every pass at its own count, every survivor and key-hit charge), so the covariance of the components and the online screen charges (4 + 183 per draw, 3 per discarded draw) are inside it. Sample: 1,080 pre-declared windows, seeds 802060-803139, 2^26 walk evaluations, screen on, k4 on, all 1,080 present: Appendix D's 720 and 360 (each seed range recorded before its run; the first record names margins on the work law as a purpose). All 1,080 ran at the shipped cap 944; Appendix B's 60 (run at d3a46ae6's cap 1,024) are history and not in the sample. Mean 589,534,035.0, s.d. 5,316,658.6, min 569,954,170, max 609,793,496 (the 720: mean 589,437,467.7; the 360: mean 589,727,169.4). H6 model: the screened window totals are i.i.d. over windows and the normal-theory Student-t and chi-square bounds hold for their mean and s.d. One-sided 99.75% bound on the mean, t(1079, 0.9975) = 2.812820: 589,989,095.1, used as 589,989,096; one-sided 99.75% bound on the s.d., chi-square(1079, 0.0025) = 953.181: 5,656,683.8; jointly 99.5%. The model checked on the 1,080 totals: skewness -0.096, excess kurtosis 0.053, Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.53; the 99.75% quantile of 100,000 bootstrap means (numpy default_rng(20261113), seeds in order) is 589,990,807, below the cap. These are bounds on the mean and s.d. of the window distribution, not a maximum over windows. K = 10,351 = ceil(589,989,096 / 57,003.18 = 10,350.11). Cap per window 10,351 x 57,003.18 = 590,039,916.18: margin 50,820.18 operations per window over the bound on the mean. For independent windows, Chebyshev on the sum over B = 2^76.388008 windows (about 9.887e22) bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows by s^2 / (B x margin^2) = 1.3e-19, below the 2^-40 slack inside lambda. Distinct claws per window over the 1,080: mean 57,032.29 (s.d. 227.44), one-sided 99.75% lower bound 57,012.83, at least C_W = 57,003.18. The harness (winmeasure_rival.py) restores the counter around its non-charging yield hooks, so they add no priced work. The import assertion also checks K >= 589,534,035 / 57,003.18 = 10,342.13: a panel-mean sanity check of the observed mean cost per claw, not a separate upper bound; H6 supplies the cap justification.
- **The claw cap m_max = 944 binds in some windows.** In 3 of the 60 Appendix B windows (run at the cap 1,024) more than 944 distinct F9 claws were evaluated (at most 959); in 108 of the 1,080 Appendix D windows (run at 944) the cap was reached; the organizer windows hold at most 11. Where it binds, the program evaluates fewer claws along the same walk: the work can only fall (H6 above is measured on the 1,080 windows, all at the cap 944), and the trial count takes min(D_i, 944) per window (Section 7), so no claw beyond the cap is counted in the trials. (0b62ed88's unscreened trial count, not used here, took min(m_w, 1,024) over its 48 windows; none reached 1,024, maximum 969.) **The last window.** The cap is checked between windows; one window's k4 work is at most 944 x (143,633 + 62,400 x (5,215 + 49,472)) operations by the claw cap (every lane a survivor with 8 classes and a key hit), and the whole screened window total was at most 609,793,496 operations in the 1,080 windows; even 1,000 times that plus the k4 bound keeps one window under 2^42 operations, 2^42 / 2,812 compressions, which is added to the total charged work (Section 5) and to the program's time assertion.

One-sided 99% bound on the loss: -0.014 - 2.473 x 0.023 = -0.071 bit, so a loss above 0.071 bit is excluded at 99%. Sensitivity: in the attack every trial has a0 even and W1 odd (class 01); the pool arms back-solve W1 with either parity, and the class-01-only paired figure is -0.021. Real variants of either fibre do not do worse than the shipped draws (R 3cc9eebe - adv: +0.023, s.e. 0.032). Row survival 25/24, 26/25, 27/26, 28/27 equal within noise. - **Key-weighted arm K (participant-run, w15/tail/mkpoolk.c, armk.sh, analyzek.py).** Per proposal: a claw drawn uniformly from the F9 claws of window 1000 + i - 15 of the shipped program (run i), and a distinct (a2, kappa) key drawn uniformly from the list, kept if the key has a mate passing F8 in that claw; the proposed words are those of its designated mate, the lowest-a3 class passing F8 (ascending a3 is the order in which k4q tests them). So (claw, key) is uniform over the pairs in which the key is a trial, as the hit keys of the attack are (every trial key is hit with the same probability 2^-32), and the proposal is the designated mate's pair, which the program compresses at every hit of that key; no reweighting and no premise on mates. Same ids r39-tail-15..42, same SMC carrier as R, every hit verified and its (a0..a3) recovered. Result: mean 2^-74.3734, one-sided 99% bound 2^-74.4662, **one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5035** (Student t, 27 df, 3.421); class-01 only (2 x c01) 2^-74.3528, its 99.9% bound 2^-74.4887. Weighted by the number of evaluated claws of each run's window (the attack weights windows by their trials): mean 2^-74.3747, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5058; correlation of window size and run tail -0.19. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1). Paired against the entry-weighted R arm (same carrier): +0.0047 bit (s.e. 0.0172). Accepted keys had 1.1857 F8-passing mates on average in the first run.

**Transfer to the new fibre.** Priced directly on the new fibre, the R 3cc9eebe arm alone (28 runs, mean -74.3781) has the one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4804 (Student t, 27 df, 3.421), above the replica's check value 2^-74.54. The R-arm claws came from windows of the shifted walk of an earlier build (previous seat's tools; seed 1000 gave 908 F9 claws there against 871 in the shipped program's window 1000), so the arm uses real F9 claws of the same walk map but not the shipped program's own windows. The figure that matches the attack exactly would be the class-01-only paired one, and it is inside the same bound.

## 9. Advice construction and preprocessing (H3)
As in w13 Section 9: the pair of 5f8e6192, chosen among 93 candidate pairs; 93 x 2^36 = 2^42.5392 constructions plus 93 x 14 x 2^24 = 2^34.35 screens, 2^42.545 in all, declared as preprocessing_log2 = 43 and added to the claimed time. The organizer experiment runs the fibre search on the shipped pair (g16_fibre_size = 2, g17_fibre_size = 1, fibre_dfs_ops = 1,944) and the 256-candidate slice (advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411). The list is built at import inside K4_SETUP; the choice of the fibre is a one-time offline search: about 7,000 fibres scored (at most 2^36 operations), five enumerated exhaustively by enum15 (per fibre 2^32 F11 tests of about 20 operations, 2^36.3, plus the real two-message trail at four points on at most 1.8 x 10^8 F10-passing solutions at about 10^3 operations each, 2^39.4; five fibres 2^41.8), their F8 counts on about 950 real claws each (9.7 x 10^6 entries x 50 operations per claw, 2^38.7 each, 2^41.0 for five) and one window per fibre: at most 2^42.6 operations, 2^31.1 compressions in all (EST from the tools' loop counts), against the 2^41.1 compressions left between the 2^42.545 of the advice and the declared 2^43.

## 10. Premises, and the limits of their evidence
- **H1-screen (new, MODEL, declared heuristic; score-setting).** Under the screened chaining-value and window law of the shipped program (S <= 5, KCAP = 679, DTRY = 8,192, KTRY = 32; production window 2^26 walk evaluations): (i) the distinct claws per window have mean 57,003.18 (the 60-window panel mean of Appendix B, s.d. 210.99), the unit C_W of B and of the cap; (ii) [this entry: the trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10679.3 per distinct claw, measured in Section 7 on the claws of the panel windows 802000-802015 with the F9 claws per window, min(D_i, 944), of the 1,080 windows of Appendix D]; (iii) kept chaining values are independent across windows; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-key count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11, hence F8, do not depend on the chaining value); the W17 claw constants (w, c) are uniform and independent of (a0, u), as H5 uses. This is a new premise of ae2d3c1c, kept: 9,044.1 (a26bcf74's keys figure, not used by this entry; its trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10679.3 by the same joint bound on the entries of the 2,000 claws of windows 802000-802015, Section 7) is the joint one-sided 99% lower bound of a26bcf74's Section 7, from the keys per F9 claw measured on 0b62ed88's unscreened claws (one-way ANOVA of the 2,000 claws' key counts over their 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df) and the distinct F9 claws per window measured on the 60 screened windows, with C_W as the declared model mean; the screen conditions the chaining value on S <= 5, so the unscreened law does not transfer by itself; the premise declares it. Support (participant-run, paired, same seeds on both builds; 16 seed pairs, 2^24 walk evaluations, harness winmeasure_rival.py; N = F8-passing listed entries and K = distinct keys among them over the four diagnostic groups 0, 50, 100, 150 of k4f, per distinct claw C): unscreened N/C 106.91, K/C 98.56; screened N/C 111.16, K/C 102.24; paired N/C change +0.0552 bit (s.e. 0.0459). Distinct F9 claws per window: 907.17 (s.d. 25.68) in the 60 screened 2^26 windows against 898.62 in the 48 unscreened ones. This probe supports a nonnegative transfer of the yield; it is not a 2^26 panel of the key count, and the transfer of the unscreened keys-per-F9-claw count to the screened law is the declared premise.
- **H1-ops.** The constants of Sections 3 and 5; the pass is a constant of the program; the screen charges 4 + 183 per draw and 3 per discarded draw.
- **H2-entries (MODEL premise of this entry; screened scope).** p_entry >= 2^-74.4783 for an F8-passing listed entry of class 01 drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, entry) triples of the attack, windows drawn under the screened law and weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 hit: the lower of the 14-run organizer pooled and class-01 means of r39-mate (Section 8; 2^-74.4594 and 2^-74.4783), rounded down. A mean of organizer-executed runs, carried to the screened window law and the whole attack, not a lower confidence bound. a26bcf74's H2-transfer (2^-74.3238, keys, designated mate; ae2d3c1c's) is cited only as the keys value; arm J (2^-74.3828) is participant-run support. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1).
- **H3-advice-construction.** As in w13; for every listed entry of the new fibre both messages follow the advice trail through step 15 (enum15 on all entries; the organizer run on one entry of every group).
- **H5-group-independence (screened-window scope).** For the windows of the screened law: windows independent (fresh first blocks, each drawn and screened independently); trials are distinct keys with an entry in F8, trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10679.3 per distinct claw (Section 7); each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw; events of different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1-screen. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and family-wise over all keys (alpha = 0.001) E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 1.36e-2. Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 1.341e-3 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise over all keys at alpha = 0.001). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the designated-mate tail events, as for the hit events themselves. 37 real 2^-32 key hits were observed against 38.58 expected (Section 7).
- **H7-mate-row19 (new; named premise H-W3-uniform).** Given a hit, its W3 is uniform over 2^32 (H-W3-uniform). With the exhaustive enumeration of Section 7 (Appendix D: a mate with offset d can follow the advice through row 19 only if W3 lies in B_d, |B_d| <= 120,832), the expected number of a hit's other F8-passing mates that do so is at most eps = 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = 1.9693e-04. Organizer test: the r39-mate manifest predicts at most two of the 1,888 hits' W3 in the union of the B_d (observed 0) and a per-bit chi-square below 62.49 (observed 24.7). Without the premise, the strict 99% cluster bound gives eps 0.12015 and time 94.1835 (disclosed, not priced). Limitation: the r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state and claw law, one listed entry per batch; the test is carried to the attack's screened claws as the entries tail is (H2-entries).
- **H6-cap-completion.** Section 7: the screened whole-window bound on 1,080 predeclared windows (Appendix D), a model-based 99.75% bound on the mean (and on the s.d.) of the screened window work under the stated window-distribution model, checked by moments, Shapiro-Wilk and a bootstrap; K = 10,351.
- **H-implicit-distinct-key-dispersion.** Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event over all keys of four groups in every F9 claw (Section 11).
- **Limits of the evidence.** The cap sample is 1,080 predeclared screened windows of the shipped program law on public seeds, all at the cap 944 (Appendix D); the trial count uses the entries of 2,000 claws of 16 Appendix B windows (802000-802015) with the F9 claws per window of the 1,080: participant-run, carried to the screened law by H1-screen as a26bcf74's keys count is. The tail and the mate test are organizer-executed (r39-mate-01..14); the tail is a mean of those runs, not a lower confidence bound. The r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state law with the claw model for (a0, a1), not from screened claws; their tail and W3 count are carried to the attack's screened claws as H2-entries states. The rows-18-19 enumeration is participant-run (Appendix D). The organizer run counts F8-passing keys and their scaled dispersion on four fixed groups of the 200 (22 claws); it is a spot test at probability 2^-7 and does not establish independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and all windows, which remains the premise H5. The memory claim is a peak over phases. No full collision has been executed; every experiment is a component test.

## 11. Experiments (organizer sandbox; every organizer-run value is hard-asserted by the program)
- `r39-transplant-claw`, trial 0: the advice collides under 39 steps; the advice-construction checks of Section 9; and for the sample entry of each of the 200 groups at the advice point: the rule holds, W9 = advice W9 + 0x05cefde0, W16 one value, both messages follow the advice trail through step 16 and message 1 the advice states from A[8], E[12] (200 of 200). Every further trial: a random chaining value and claw-free (a0, u) with a listed entry of the fibre: transplant states, W1 = u and W16 - g = F(u) - F(a0).
- `r39k4-window-small`, trials 0-3: windows of 2^21 evaluations, check mode, k4 on for every F9 claw (7, 11, 4, 1 claws). Every claw asserts W9 = C9 + HD - a1 = W9 of a listed entry and W16 = g. The pass runs over all 62,400 lanes. Asserted tuples (claws, F9, 0, pass lanes, survivors, key hits, k4 ops, total ops): (233,7,0,436800,2,0,1019221,11504962), (222,11,0,624000,5,0,1454268,13875066), (256,4,0,249600,2,0,584630,13031225), (232,1,0,62400,0,0,144113,11245985). Each k4 ops value is (evaluated F9 claws, pass lanes / 62,400) x (143,633 + 480), plus 12 per repeated F9 claw (the dedupe lookup), plus 10,430 for its 2 real survivors; 13,126 for its 5 real survivors; 8,178 for its 2 real survivors. Each trial emits k4_setup = 1,107,473,556.
  - The four asserted windows run with the screen off (`screen=0`; the k4 path is the same code with the screen on or off), so their tuples are 0b62ed88's.
  - Pass-off control: trials 0 and 1 are re-run with k4 off; claws and F9 equal, ops_off = ops - k4_ops.
  - Screened window (trial 0, same seed, screen on as on the attack path): asserted that the window is not skipped, the kept chaining value has S <= 5, every draw is charged 187 operations (kept) or 190 (discarded), and the discarded-draw count equals the number of draws with S > 5. On the organizer seed of trial 0: 12 draws, 11 discarded, kept S = 1, (claws, F9, total ops) = (258, 1, 10,371,107). No new output key.
  - Planted check on the first F9 claw of each window, for each of the 200 groups: the key is found and its counted cost is asserted.
  - Key dispersion over all entries of every 50th group (4 groups), all F9 claws: per claw D = keys with an entry in F8, K = those whose W17 x 2654435761 mod 2^32 has its top 7 bits zero (probability 2^-7). Asserted per trial (sum D, sum K, Pearson, claws): (59,256, 437, 6.5188, 7); (67,492, 518, 7.9839, 10); (17,882, 142, 0.7772, 4); (1,872, 7, 4.0067, 1). Pooled 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws. Acceptance region, asserted on the sums: sum D >= 96,821, |sum K - sum D/128| within 2.576 s.d., Pearson < 40.29 (99% quantile, 22 dof).
- `r39-tail-01..14` (not in this manifest): w13's replica (experiments/r39tail.py in earlier entries) is the first part of the bare raw-string statement that ends experiments/r39joint_k4.py, byte-identical but for its final main-guard line, because the verifier admits only the files that the manifest runs and the organizer runs each program alone as /input/program.py (so no experiment can import another file); trial 0 of every r39-mate run calls its verify_smc_stats(QDECL), so the replica's calibration (c18 = 206) and its 14-run table with the asserted bounds are executed in every run.
- `r39-mate-01..14` (new, program experiments/r39joint_k4.py; all 14 in the manifest): the replica and the mate code are the bare raw-string statement that ends experiments/r39joint_k4.py (plain source; the compiler drops a bare string, so the attack holds no copy of it and its memory ledger is unchanged); for these ids serve() reads that text back from its own file and runs it with exec in a fresh namespace {L: this module, Q_: the request}, so it reads the k4 list and routines from L; the attack path and the other two experiments never touch it. Under the organizer isolation every run keeps well clear of the 128 MB cap (Section 8 timing line); the unchanged replica; one uniform listed entry per batch of 2,048 lanes (4 kappa groups per run drawn proportional to size and asserted against the rule's enumeration), the lanes' W8, W9 the replica's own draws; 6 chunks x 80 batches. Every collision verified by the replica's own verify(), its class counted, its chaining value and message recovered and reproduced by k4_words, its W3 recorded; every F8-passing mate of the same key recompressed on the same claw and traced row by row. Predictions on the reported W3 (checked from the observations, not asserted in code): over the 14 runs at most two hits have W3 in the union of the B_d of Appendix D (expected 0.24 if W3 were uniform; falsified at 3 or more), and the per-bit chi-square of the hits' W3 is below 62.49 on 32 df (the 99.9% point); observed 0 and 24.7. Hard-asserted: the prediction (no mate past row 19), the group sizes, the replica's calibration and table, and each run's replay digest (the first 48 bits of the sha256 of the run's full record, reported as the observation digest48 and listed in the per-run table of Section 8; the record is printed in Appendix E). Totals: 1,888 hits (class 01: 466), 638 F8-passing mates, first deviation at row 18 for 335 and row 19 for 303, none later.

## Appendix D. The rows-18-19 enumeration (participant-run; row19_proof/row19x.c and adv.h, verbatim)

P(w) below is the explicit set of conditions: with the advice states through row 17 fixed (adv.h, generated from the replica's advice trace), W18 = w must give the advice's XOR differences of A and E after row 18 (TA22, TE22), and the row-19 modular E difference must be one of +-2^19 +-2^5 with a matching A difference. B_d is the set of W3 with Delta(W3, d) = s0(W3 + d) - s0(W3) - d a nonzero element of D = P - P. Output (row19x.out, sha256 88005a11...): |P| = 65,536, |D| = 9,427,275; per offset, the size of B_d as in Section 7.

```c
/* adv.h */
static const unsigned AX[24]={0x90ccc398u,0xd0a84bfdu,0x65c5bb49u,0xaa79ff87u,0xdc27bd7eu,0xedd22c6bu,0x4773552bu,0x251f3c14u,0x972ee2f4u,0x58bdaecbu,0x759f7065u,0xcc8f1219u,0x2af1c95eu,0xc76d0d7bu,0x25b9a00eu,0xca0aecd2u,0x5829bcdbu,0xbf5e1f93u,0xbd4f5653u,0x269f8f4fu,0xcc8fd4cbu,0xce7b54b4u,0xd4f95672u,0xfff8cabfu};
static const unsigned EX[24]={0xaa1ed4d5u,0xb1af5ec5u,0x4ff7998au,0xfac64fb6u,0x9aad52c2u,0x1009c407u,0xf02b08c9u,0x4c53ba63u,0x78ecacdfu,0xb56b936cu,0x5104937fu,0xf8608614u,0x85dbb23du,0xac230e77u,0x9e3b6fedu,0xff00f835u,0xbc4a3994u,0xa87dbd19u,0x9dca05a5u,0xd2c3ec33u,0x9776869eu,0x771adf7eu,0x483e6228u,0x75abcc17u};
static const unsigned AY[24]={0x90ccc398u,0xd0a84bfdu,0x65c5bb49u,0xaa79ff87u,0xdc27bd7eu,0xedd22c6bu,0x4773552bu,0x251f3c14u,0x972ee2f4u,0x58bdaecbu,0x759f7065u,0xcc8f1219u,0x6af1c95eu,0xcfe71c5bu,0x25b9a00eu,0xca0aecd2u,0x5ce9bcdbu,0x96179b98u,0xfd4b5673u,0x36998e6fu,0xc98ed4cbu,0xce7b54b4u,0x94f95672u,0xfff8cabfu};
static const unsigned EY[24]={0xaa1ed4d5u,0xb1af5ec5u,0x4ff7998au,0xfac64fb6u,0x9aad52c2u,0x1009c407u,0xf02b08c9u,0x4c53ba63u,0x78ecacdfu,0xb56b936cu,0x5104937fu,0xf8608614u,0xc5dbb23du,0xa49b1e57u,0x3f1b2107u,0xb708f935u,0xf8883994u,0x82412611u,0x9dca05a5u,0xc2c3ec33u,0x9776879eu,0xf798437fu,0x483e6228u,0x75a3cc37u};
static const unsigned K18=0x0fc19dc6u,K19=0x240ca1ccu,W18A=0xaa128b2eu,W19A=0x85c7fdabu;
static const unsigned TA22=0x40000000u,TE22=0x00000000u,TA23=0x00000000u,TE23=0x00080020u;
```

```c
/* row19x.c: exhaustive check that no mate of a colliding entry can follow the advice through row 19.
   (1) P = {W18 : rows 18-19 admit the advice differences, states through row 17 = advice}, by enumeration of 2^32.
   (2) D = P - P (bitset over 2^32).
   (3) For every mate offset d in delta_set.bin (all b3 - a3 over listed entries of one key) and every W3 in 2^32:
       Delta = s0(W3+d) - s0(W3) - d (the mate's W18 minus the hit's). A mate can pass row 19 only if Delta in D.
   Counts Delta == 0 separately (then rows 18 coincide and row 19 is decided by W19). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "adv.h"
typedef uint32_t u32; typedef uint64_t u64;
#define ROR(x,k) (((x)>>(k))|((x)<<(32-(k))))
static inline u32 S0(u32 x){return ROR(x,2)^ROR(x,13)^ROR(x,22);}
static inline u32 S1(u32 x){return ROR(x,6)^ROR(x,11)^ROR(x,25);}
static inline u32 s0(u32 x){return ROR(x,7)^ROR(x,18)^(x>>3);}
static inline u32 CH(u32 e,u32 f,u32 g){return (e&f)^(~e&g);}
static inline u32 MJ(u32 a,u32 b,u32 c){return (a&b)^(a&c)^(b&c);}
static int P(u32 w){
  u32 ex=AX[18]+EX[18]+S1(EX[21])+CH(EX[21],EX[20],EX[19])+K18+w, ey=AY[18]+EY[18]+S1(EY[21])+CH(EY[21],EY[20],EY[19])+K18+w;
  u32 ax=ex-AX[18]+S0(AX[21])+MJ(AX[21],AX[20],AX[19]), ay=ey-AY[18]+S0(AY[21])+MJ(AY[21],AY[20],AY[19]);
  if((ax^ay)!=TA22||(ex^ey)!=TE22) return 0;
  u32 fx=AX[19]+EX[19]+S1(ex)+CH(ex,EX[21],EX[20])+K19, fy=AY[19]+EY[19]+S1(ey)+CH(ey,EY[21],EY[20])+K19, DE=fy-fx;
  u32 gx=-AX[19]+S0(ax)+MJ(ax,AX[21],AX[20]), gy=-AY[19]+S0(ay)+MJ(ay,AY[21],AY[20]);
  if(DE+gy-gx) return 0;
  return DE==(u32)(-(1u<<19)+(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)((1u<<19)+(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)((1u<<19)-(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)(-(1u<<19)-(1u<<5));
}
static u32 L[1<<17];
int main(){
  int nL=0; for(u64 W=0;W<(1ull<<32);W++){u32 w=(u32)W;if(P(w))L[nL++]=w;}
  printf("|P| = %d\n",nL); fflush(stdout);
  u64*D=calloc(1ull<<26,8); if(!D){printf("alloc\n");return 2;}
  for(int i=0;i<nL;i++){u32 a=L[i];for(int j=0;j<nL;j++){u32 d=L[j]-a;D[d>>6]|=1ull<<(d&63);}}
  u64 nd=0;for(u64 i=0;i<(1ull<<26);i++)nd+=__builtin_popcountll(D[i]);
  printf("|D| = |P-P| = %llu (2^%.3f)\n",nd,__builtin_log2((double)nd)); fflush(stdout);
  /* low-residue filter mod 2^23 */
  u64*F=calloc(1u<<17,8);for(u64 i=0;i<(1ull<<26);i++)if(D[i]){u64 m=D[i];while(m){int b=__builtin_ctzll(m);m&=m-1;u32 d=(u32)(i*64+b);F[(d&0x7fffff)>>6]|=1ull<<(d&63);}}
  u64 nf=0;for(int i=0;i<(1<<17);i++)nf+=__builtin_popcountll(F[i]);printf("residues mod 2^23 covered: %llu of 8388608\n",nf);fflush(stdout);
  FILE*f=fopen("delta_set.bin","rb");u32 ds[64];int nds=(int)fread(ds,4,64,f);fclose(f);
  printf("mate offsets d: %d\n",nds);
  u64 tot_in=0,tot_zero=0;
  for(int k=0;k<nds;k++){u32 d=ds[k];u64 in=0,zero=0;u32 ex_in=0,ex_zero=0;
    for(u64 W=0;W<(1ull<<32);W++){u32 w=(u32)W;u32 Dl=s0(w+d)-s0(w)-d;
      if(!Dl){if(!zero)ex_zero=w;zero++;continue;}
      if(!((F[(Dl&0x7fffff)>>6]>>(Dl&63))&1))continue;
      if((D[Dl>>6]>>(Dl&63))&1){if(!in)ex_in=w;in++;}}
    printf("d=%08x  Delta in D (nonzero): %llu%s  Delta==0: %llu%s\n",d,in,in?"":"",zero,"");
    if(in)printf("   e.g. W3=%08x\n",ex_in); if(zero)printf("   e.g. W3=%08x (Delta 0)\n",ex_zero);
    fflush(stdout);tot_in+=in;tot_zero+=zero;}
  printf("TOTAL over all d and all W3: Delta in D\{0}: %llu ; Delta == 0: %llu\n",tot_in,tot_zero);
  return 0;}
```

## Appendix E. The full record of each r39-mate run (W3 values included), pinned by its organizer-recorded digest48

The organizer's runner records only numeric observations, so each r39-mate run reports eight: log2_carrier, hits, mates, mates_f8, through19, carrier_w18_clusters, cluster_sum_sq and digest48. digest48 is the first 48 bits of the sha256 of the run's full record, the JSON text after the run id on each line below (Python json.dumps with sort_keys=True and default separators); the program hard-asserts the same 48 bits for each id (X_), so a run that reproduces the recorded digest48 reproduces this record: ks, groups, first_deviation_row, cluster_sizes, cls and w3 (every hit's W3, in hit order). The bad-set count and the per-bit chi-square of Section 7 are computed from these W3 values.
